sections.title: 英语知识运用
sections.directions: Directions: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: In our contemporary culture, the prospect of communicating with – or even looking at – a stranger is virtually unbearable. Everyone around us seems to agree by the way they cling to their phones, even without a
on a subway. It's a sad reality – our desire to avoid interacting with other human beings – because there's
to be gained from talking to the stranger standing by you. But you wouldn't know it,
into your phone. This universal protection sends the
: "Please don't approach me." What is it that makes us feel we need to hide
our screens? One answer is fear, according to Jon Wortmann, an executive mental coach. We fear rejection, or that our innocent social advances will be
as "weird." We fear we'll be
. We fear we'll be disruptive. Strangers are inherently
to us, so we are more likely to feel
when communicating with them compared with our friends and acquaintances. To avoid this uneasiness, we
to our phones. "Phones become our security blanket," Wortmann says. "They are our happy glasses that protect us from what we perceive is going to be more
." But once we rip off the band-aid, tuck our smartphones in our pockets and look up, it doesn't
so bad. In one 2011 experiment, behavioral scientists Nicholas Epley and Juliana Schroeder asked commuters to do the unthinkable: Start a

how they would feel after talking to a stranger, the commuters thought their

questions.analysis: signal 【线索】地铁里没信号也照刷手机 线索是本句的场景：they cling to their phones, even without a __(1)__ on a 种'信号'。 【选项】 A) signal ✓ 手机+地铁＝最典型缺'信号' signal 指手机信号，与 cling to their phones 和 on a subway 严丝合缝——地铁里常没信号， B) permit ✗ 搭配勉强、与场景无关 C) ticket ✗ 易选项：忽略了手机这条线索 ticket = 车票，'地铁里没票'乍看也通，但本句的主语是 they cling to their phones，强调对手机 D) record ✗ 语义无关 【验证】代回后整句意思：they cling to their phones, even without a __(1)__ on a subway → 即

much 【线索】作者立场：和陌生人聊有收获 本句开头 It's a sad reality – our desire to avoid interacting with other human beings – because there's __(2)__ to be gained from talking to the stranger standing by you，'sad reality + because' 已经表明作者认为'回避是可惜的，因为本可以从交流中获 益'；而第七段 Talking to strangers can make you feel connected 也呼应这一立场—— 【选项】A) nothing ✗ 立场反了 nothing 意为'什么也得不到'，那 sad reality 就无从谈起——既然得不到，回避就不是 sad 了。与 B) little ✗ 极性同样为负，方向反了 little 表'几乎没有'，与 nothing 同向，否定交流的价值，与全文'交谈有益'相悖。 C) another ✗ 代词指代落空 D) much ✓ 正向、与全文立场吻合 much 表'很多东西可得'，正是 sad reality 的依据：本可得 much，却因为回避而错失，逻辑 【验证】代回后：因为本可以从与陌生人交谈中获得 much（很多），所以回避才显得 sad；与第七 段结论 Talking to strangers can make you feel connected 完全呼应。

plugged 【线索】你埋头进手机里，所以浑然不觉 线索是 But you wouldn't know it, __(3)__ into your phone：'但你不会知道，因为你 ___ 进手机里'。前一句讲'本可以从交谈中收获很多'，这里用 you wouldn't know it 反推：你 【选项】A) beaten ✗ 义不对、搭配生硬 beaten 意为'被打败、击败'，beaten into 多用于 beaten into submission 之类，与'埋头看手 B) plugged ✓ 固定隐喻：plugged into = 沉浸于 plugged into 字面是'插入'，常用隐喻为'专注沉浸于（电子设备/某话题）'，与 your phone 搭 配是地道用法，恰好解释了 you wouldn't know it。 C) guided ✗ 施动对象错位 D) brought ✗ 搭配虽通但语义虚 brought into 意为'被带入'，没有 plugged into 那种'沉浸专注'的隐喻力度，与上文 wouldn't 【验证】代回后：But you wouldn't know it, __(3)__ into your phone = 但因为你正埋头沉浸在 手机里，所以察觉不到——句意通顺，且呼应第一段 cling to their phones 的'依赖手

message 【线索】冒号后是完整一句话内容 This universal protection sends the __(4)__: "Please don't approach me."——冒号后给 【选项】 A) message ✓ send the message + 引号话内容 message 表传达的'信息内容'，send the message: "..." 是地道搭配，完美呼应冒号后那句 'Please don't approach me'。 B) code ✗ 编码义不符 C) notice ✗ 公示通告义偏书面 notice 多指张贴的'通告/通知'，搭配上更常用 put up a notice 或 give notice；用 send the D) sign ✗ 搭配错位 sign 作名词常用 give/show a sign，send a sign 不地道；且 sign 指'迹象/标志'，不能直接以一 【验证】代回后：手机这层 universal protection 在向外界发送一条 message：'请别靠近我'。语

behind 【线索】屏幕是用来挡住自己的 What is it that makes us feel we need to hide __(5)__ our screens?——'屏幕'是被用来 作为遮挡物的，我们藏在它'背后'。再结合 This universal protection 的'保护层'比喻，屏幕 【选项】A) under ✗ 屏幕不会盖在头上 B) beyond ✗ '越过'与遮挡相反 beyond = 在……之外/超越，与'躲在屏幕后面'语义相反。 C) behind ✓ hide behind = 躲在……后 behind 与 hide 构成最常见搭配，意为'躲在屏幕后面'，正契合第二段把手机比作 protection 的 D) from ✗ hide from 后接'躲避对象' 【验证】代回后：we need to hide __(5)__ our screens? = 我们需要躲在屏幕后面，与全文'用手机

misinterpreted 【线索】我们怕善意的搭话被解读成'怪异' We fear rejection, or that our innocent social advances will be __(6)__ as "weird."——'innocent social advances ... as weird' 表示'本无恶意的搭话被对方理解成怪 异'。'被理解为' 正是 misinterpret as 的核心义。 【选项】A) misapplied ✗ 误用——对象是方法/规则 misapplied 表'误用、用错地方'，宾语应是 rule/method/funds 之类；'搭话被误用为怪异'语义 B) misinterpreted ✓ misinterpret … as = 被解读为 misinterpreted 即'被错误解读'，misinterpret X as Y 是固定框架，把'本无恶意的搭话'误解 为'怪异'，与上文'fear rejection'的情绪链完全一致。 C) misadjusted ✗ 误调——对象是机器/参数 misadjusted 意为'调整不当'，宾语多是仪器/姿势，与 'social advances' 搭不上。 D) mismatched ✗ 误配——讲不通'被误配为怪异' mismatched 表'不匹配/错配'，多用于双方对照（color mismatched），不能接 as 'weird' 这种 【验证】代回后：我们害怕善意的搭话会被对方 misinterpreted 为'怪人'——情绪（fear）+ 解读对

judged 【线索】三个 We fear 并列，本题为社交担忧 We fear we'll be __(7)__. We fear we'll be disruptive.——前句怕被 misinterpreted as 社交担忧。be judged（被评判）正合此意。 【选项】 A) judged ✓ 怕被人品头论足，社交担忧链最契合 judged 指'被评判、被指指点点'，与 misinterpreted as weird、disruptive 三句构成同一情绪 B) fired ✗ 脱离社交语境 C) replaced ✗ 对象错位 D) delayed ✗ 无关情绪线 delayed = 被耽搁，与情绪、评价无关。 【验证】代回后：we fear we'll be judged = 我们怕被人评判，与前后两句构成'怕被解读为怪/怕被

unfamiliar 【线索】陌生人本质上对我们是'不熟悉的' Strangers are inherently __(8)__ to us, so we are more likely to feel __(9)__ when communicating with them compared with our friends and acquaintances.——句末与 friends and acquaintances（熟人）形成对比，反推空位应表达'不熟悉'，即 unfamiliar。 【选项】A) unreasonable ✗ 义不符 unreasonable = 不讲道理，给陌生人贴这个标签过于负面，也与下文 'friends and acquaintances' 的对比逻辑无关。 B) ungrateful ✗ 情感关系不对位 C) unconventional ✗ 义偏'反常规'，不对应'不熟悉' unconventional = 非常规的、不落俗套的，与'陌生人是否熟悉'无关，且不与 friends/acquaintances 形成对照。 D) unfamiliar ✓ stranger 的同义内核：陌生＝不熟 unfamiliar = 不熟悉的，正是 stranger 的内核义，与 friends and acquaintances 形成漂亮的 对比，因果链 'inherently unfamiliar → feel anxious' 顺。 【验证】代回后：陌生人对我们天生就是不熟悉的，所以和他们交流比和熟人交流更让人不安——下 接第 9 题 'anxious' 的因果链完美承接。

anxious 【线索】feel + 与 fear 同向的负面情绪 we are more likely to feel __(9)__ when communicating with them + 后文 To avoid this uneasiness——'this uneasiness（这种不安）' 就是空位情绪的同义复现，指向 anxious（焦虑/不安）。 【选项】A) comfortable ✗ 极性反了 comfortable = 自在的，是正向情绪，与下文 this uneasiness 与全段 fear 主线相反。 B) confident ✗ 正向情绪，反方向 confident = 自信的，同为正向情绪，与 fear/uneasiness 不符。 C) anxious ✓ 焦虑＝uneasiness 的同义 anxious = 焦虑/不安，正好被下一句 To avoid this uneasiness 同义复现确认，与全段 fear 主 D) angry ✗ 情绪类型错 angry = 愤怒，虽然也是负面情绪，但与 fear/uneasiness（恐惧/不安）属不同情绪类别，且全文 【验证】代回后：feel anxious → To avoid this uneasiness（用 anxious 解释 uneasiness），上

turn 【线索】为了躲不安，我们转向手机求助 To avoid this uneasiness, we __(10)__ to our phones.——目的状语 To avoid... 表明动作 是'求助/依赖'类；turn to 是固定搭配。下一句 Phones become our security blanket 也 【选项】A) attend ✗ 义不对 attend to = 处理/照料，宾语多为'事务、患者'，与'求助手机'语义不符。 B) turn ✓ turn to = 求助/依赖 turn to 是固定搭配，表'转而依靠'，与 To avoid this uneasiness 和 Phones become our security blanket 两句无缝呼应。 C) take ✗ 搭配生硬 D) point ✗ 义不通 point to = 指向，主语应是事物/证据，而非主动'求助'。 【验证】代回后：To avoid this uneasiness, we turn to our phones. → 为了躲避不安，我们求助/ 依赖手机；与下一句把手机比作 security blanket 完美承接。

dangerous 【线索】保护 us → 免遭'危险' Phones become our security blanket. They are our happy glasses that protect us from what we perceive is going to be more __(11)__.——security blanket、protect 【选项】 A) dangerous ✓ protect from + dangerous 严丝合缝 dangerous 与 security blanket、protect us 构成完整逻辑链：手机是安全毯，让我们觉得外界 B) mysterious ✗ 强度不够、性质不对 mysterious = 神秘的，并不一定是威胁，未必需要 security blanket 来防御。 C) violent ✗ 过强、出离全文语境 violent = 暴力的，把'和陌生人搭话'的社交不安升格成暴力威胁，与全文 fear of judgment 的细 D) boring ✗ 不需要 protection boring = 无聊，无聊不需要 security blanket 来保护；与 protect from 的逻辑不通。 【验证】代回后：手机像安全毯，保护我们免受'我们感觉会更 dangerous' 的外界——与全段'陌生

hurt 【线索】撕掉创可贴的隐喻：其实没那么疼 But once we rip off the band-aid, tuck our smartphones in our pockets and look up, it doesn't __(12)__ so bad.——前半句用 rip off the band-aid（撕掉创可贴）作隐喻，撕 之前怕疼，撕完发现 'it doesn't hurt so bad（其实没那么疼）'——这是 it doesn't hurt 【选项】A) bend ✗ 义不通 B) resist ✗ 及物动词、缺宾语 C) hurt ✓ rip off band-aid + hurt = 经典英语隐喻 hurt 与 rip off the band-aid 构成最地道的隐喻搭配：撕创可贴前怕疼，撕完发现 'it doesn't hurt so bad'，正好引出实验结论。 D) decay ✗ 义不对 【验证】代回后：撕掉创可贴、收起手机抬起头之后，it doesn't hurt so bad → 其实没那么疼。隐

conversation 【线索】实验任务＝和陌生人开口聊聊 Nicholas Epley and Juliana Schroeder asked commuters to do the unthinkable: Start a __(13)__. 紧接下一句 They had Chicago train commuters talk to their fellow __(14)__. —— 'Start a ___' 被下一句的 talk to 直接同义复现，'talk' 对应的名词正 是 conversation。 【选项】A) lecture ✗ 单向讲授，不符合'搭话' B) debate ✗ 对抗性、不符合通勤搭话 C) conversation ✓ 对应 talk to，唯一中性双向用语 conversation = 交谈，对应下一句 talk to their fellow，与全文 talking to strangers 这条主线 D) negotiation ✗ 目的性过强、语场不符 negotiation = 谈判，需有利益博弈，通勤场景毫无相关。 【验证】代回后：Start a conversation → 让通勤者发起一次交谈，与下一句 talk to their fellow passengers 完美互译；整段实验主轴清晰。

passengers 【线索】commuters 的同身份指代＝passengers They had Chicago train commuters talk to their fellow __(14)__.——主语是 train commuters（火车通勤者），fellow ___ 应是与之同身份的'同车乘客'，即 passengers。 【选项】A) trainees ✗ 易混词陷阱：train ≠ trainee B) employees ✗ 范围过窄 employees = 雇员，未必是 commuters 的同身份——通勤者并非全是雇员（学生/退休者也 通勤）。 C) researchers ✗ 身份错位 researchers = 研究者，本文中是 Epley 和 Schroeder，与 commuters 是研究者—被试关系，不 能 fellow。 D) passengers ✓ fellow passengers = 同车乘客 passengers 与 train commuters 同身份，fellow passengers 是地道说法，指代清晰。 【验证】代回后：talk to their fellow passengers = 让通勤者和同车乘客搭话；与上句 Start a conversation 实验任务完美承接。

predict 【线索】请受试者先预测搭话后的感受 asked other people in the same train station to __(15)__ how they would feel after talking to a stranger——动词应为'预想/预测'之义，后文 the commuters thought their __(16)__ would be more pleasant if they sat on their own 用 thought 同义复现，确认 【选项】A) reveal ✗ 已发生才能 reveal B) choose ✗ 宾语类型不符 C) predict ✓ predict + how they would feel = 预测感受 predict 即'预测'，与 would feel、下一句 thought 同义复现，正是该实验的关键步骤。 D) design ✗ 义不通 design = 设计，'设计他们会怎么感受'不通。 【验证】代回后：让站内其他人预测搭话后的感受——下一句立刻给出预测内容 the commuters thought their __(16)__ would be more pleasant if they sat on their own，语义链顺。

ride 【线索】train commuters 的旅程＝乘车 ride Chicago train commuters + their __(16)__ would be more pleasant if they sat on their own——主语是火车通勤者，他们的'旅程'用 ride 最贴；sat on their own（独自坐 【选项】A) voyage ✗ 海上长程，方式不符 voyage 多指远洋长途，火车通勤用 voyage 显然不对。 B) flight ✗ 工具错 flight = 航班，与火车无关。 C) walk ✗ 工具错 walk = 步行，与 train commuters 不符；且 sat on their own 表明是坐着，不是走着。 D) ride ✓ train ride 是地道说法 ride = 乘车之旅，与 train commuters 完全对应；sat on their own 也支撑'乘车'之义。 【验证】代回后：通勤者觉得他们的 ride 若独自坐着会更愉快——下一句的实验反转 'not a single person reported having been embarrassed' 才有可比对象，逻辑顺。

went through 【线索】受试者完成了实验之后 after they __(17)__ with the experiment, "not a single person reported having been embarrassed."——after + 实验完成 + 没人感到尴尬，可见空位表'实际进行/完成了实 验'，go through with 是地道搭配。 【选项】 A) went through ✓ go through with = 把实验进行到底 B) did away ✗ do away with = 废除/取消 did away with 意为'废除/除掉'，与'完成实验'相反。 C) caught up ✗ catch up with = 赶上/追上 caught up with 多用于追上某人/某事，不表'完成实验'。 D) put up ✗ put up with = 忍受 【验证】代回后：after they went through with the experiment → 在他们把实验进行完之后，没

In fact 【线索】预期糟糕→实际更愉快：反差 前文 Though the participants didn't expect a positive experience / not a single person reported having been embarrassed 已说明事先以为糟、事后没人尴尬；本句 __(18)__, these commutes were reportedly more enjoyable compared with those without communication 是把事实进一步落地——'实际上反倒更愉快'。这种'预想 vs 实 际'的强反差，最对位的是 In fact（事实上）。 【选项】A) In turn ✗ 义为'反过来/接着'，方向不对 B) In fact ✓ In fact 引反差事实 In fact = 实际上，正是用来把'预期糟糕'与'实际更愉快'反差出来，与前句 not a single person ... embarrassed 形成顺承式反差。 C) In particular ✗ 义为'尤其'，逻辑不对 D) In consequence ✗ 义为'结果'，不是因果链 【验证】代回后：In fact, these commutes were reportedly more enjoyable... → 把'预想糟

since 【线索】实验结果由人性常识解释 these commutes were reportedly more enjoyable compared with those without communication, which makes absolute sense, __(19)__ human beings thrive off of social connections——前一分句先说'这事符合常理'（makes absolute sense），后一分 【选项】A) unless ✗ 义为'除非'，方向反 B) whereas ✗ 义为'然而'，转折不对 C) if ✗ 条件性，弱化事实 D) since ✓ since = 既然/因为（引常识） since 引出人所共知的因由，与 makes absolute sense 一气呵成：'之所以理所当然，是因为人 【验证】代回后：…which makes absolute sense, since human beings thrive off of social connections → 这事合理，因为人类本就是靠社交联结而蓬勃发展；与全文 outline 的'结

simple 【线索】结论就这么简单 It's that __(20)__: Talking to strangers can make you feel connected.——冒号后是一句 极简的结论，照应前文 it doesn't __(12)__ so bad（其实没那么糟）和 not a single person reported having been embarrassed——作者意在告诉读者：道理就这么 simple （简单）。 【选项】A) funny ✗ 感情色彩不符 B) simple ✓ It's that simple = 道理就这么简单 simple 与 'It's that ___:' 构成英文经典的'就这么简单'收束，紧扣'撕掉创可贴其实没那么疼/和陌 C) logical ✗ 义已被上句的 makes sense 占用 logical = 合乎逻辑，但前一句已经用 which makes absolute sense 表达过'合乎逻辑'之意，此处 再用 logical 是重复，且不如 simple 收束有力。 D) rare ✗ 义反、与立场冲突 【验证】代回后：It's that simple: Talking to strangers can make you feel connected. → 道理就 OVERVIEW · 通读建境 文章开篇就给全文定调：the prospect of communicating with – or even looking at – a stranger is virtually unbearable，并指出我们靠死攥手机来回避；随后第二段点出真正的核 心观点——there's __(2)__ to be gained from talking to the stranger standing by you，即和 第一段先描现象：人人捧着手机回避陌生人（cling to their phones）；第二段过渡——回 避其实让我们错过收获，手机像一张'请勿靠近'的牌（Please don't approach me）；第 们感到不安（Strangers are inherently __(8)__ to us），手机是'安全毯'；第六段引入 Epley & Schroeder 的 2011 年通勤实验，事先预想糟糕、事后反馈却完全相反（not a single person reported having been embarrassed）；第七段收束观点：和陌生人交谈反而让人感 到联结（Talking to strangers can make you feel connected）。 SENTENCE INSIGHTS · 句子精讲 8 It's a sad reality – our desire to avoid interacting with other human beings – because there's much to be gained from talking to the stranger standing by you. What is it that makes us feel we need to hide behind our screens? Strangers are inherently unfamiliar to us, so we are more likely to feel anxious when communicat...

sections.title: 阅读理解
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

blocks.content: A new study suggests that contrary to most surveys, people are actually more stressed at home than at work. Researchers measured people's cortisol, which is a stress marker, while they were at work and while they were at home and found it higher at what is supposed to be a place of refuge. "Further contradicting conventional wisdom, we found that women as well as men have lower levels of stress at work than at home," writes one of the researchers, Sarah Damaske. In fact women even say they feel better at work, she notes. "It is men, not women, who report being happier at home than at work." Another surprise is that the findings hold true for both those with children and without, but more so for nonparents. This is why people who work outside the home have better health. What the study doesn't measure is whether people are still doing work when they're at home, whether it is household work or work brought home from the office. For many men, the end of the workday is a time to kick back. For women who stay home, they never get to leave the office. And for women who work outside the home, they often are playing catch-up with household tasks. With the blurring of roles, and the fact that the home front lags well behind the workplace in making adjustments for working women, it's not surprising that women are more stressed at home. But it's not just a gender thing. At work, people pretty much know what they're supposed to be doing: working, making money, doing the tasks they have to do in order to draw an income. The bargain is very pure: Employee puts in hours of physical or mental labor and employee draws out life-sustaining moola. On the home front, however, people have no such clarity. Rare is the household in which the division of labor is so clinically and methodically laid out. There are a lot of tasks to be done, there are inadequate rewards for most of them. Your home colleagues – your family – have no clear rewards for their labor; they need to be talked into it, or if they're teenagers, threatened with complete removal of all electronic devices. Plus, they're your family. You cannot fire your family. You never really get to go home from home. So it's not surprising that people are more stressed at home. Not only are the tasks apparently infinite, the co-workers are much harder to motivate.

For years, studies have found that first-generation college students – those who do not have a parent with a college degree – lag other students on a range of education achievement factors. Their grades are lower and their dropout rates are higher. But since such students are most likely to advance economically if they succeed in higher education, colleges and universities have pushed for decades to recruit more of them. This has created "a paradox" in that recruiting first-generation students, but then watching many of them fail, means that higher education has "continued to reproduce and widen, rather than close" an achievement gap based on social class, according to the depressing beginning of a paper forthcoming in the journal Psychological Science. But the article is actually quite optimistic, as it outlines a potential solution to this problem, suggesting that an approach (which involves a one-hour, next-to-no-cost program) can close 63 percent of the achievement gap (measured by such factors as grades) between first-generation and other students. The authors of the paper are from different universities, and their findings are based on a study involving 147 students (who completed the project) at an unnamed private university. First generation was defined as not having a parent with a four-year college degree. Most of the first-generation students (59.1 percent) were recipients of Pell Grants, a federal grant for undergraduates with financial need, while this was true only for 8.6 percent of the students with at least one parent with a four-year degree. Their thesis – that a relatively modest intervention could have a big impact – was based on the view that first-generation students may be most lacking not in potential but in practical knowledge about how to deal with the issues that face most college students. They cite past research by several authors to show that this is the gap that must be narrowed to close the achievement gap. Many first-generation students "struggle to navigate the middle-class culture of higher education, learn the 'rules of the game,' and take advantage of college resources," they write. And this becomes more of a problem when colleges don't talk about the class advantages and disadvantages of different groups of students. "Because US colleges and universities seldom acknowledge how social class can affect students' educational experiences, many first-generation students lack insight about why they are struggling and do not understand how students 'like them' can improve."

Even in traditional offices, "the lingua franca of corporate America has gotten much more emotional and much more right-brained than it was 20 years ago," said Harvard Business School professor Nancy Koehn. She started spinning off examples. "If you and I parachuted back to Fortune 500 companies in 1990, we would see much less frequent use of terms like journey, mission, passion. There were goals, there were strategies, there were objectives, but we didn't talk about energy; we didn't talk about passion." Koehn pointed out that this new era of corporate vocabulary is very "team"-oriented – and not by coincidence. "Let's not forget sports – in male-dominated corporate America, it's still a big deal. It's not explicitly conscious; it's the idea that I'm a coach, and you're my team, and we're in this together. There are lots and lots of CEOs in very different companies, but most think of themselves as coaches and this is their team and they want to win." These terms are also intended to infuse work with meaning – and, as Rakesh Khurana, another professor, points out, increase allegiance to the firm. "You have the importation of terminology that historically used to be associated with non-profit organizations and religious organizations: terms like vision, values, passion, and purpose," said Khurana. This new focus on personal fulfillment can help keep employees motivated amid increasingly loud debates over work-life balance. The "mommy wars" of the 1990s are still going on today, prompting arguments about why women still can't have it all and books like Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In, whose title has become a buzzword in its own right. Terms like unplug, offline, life-hack, bandwidth, and capacity are all about setting boundaries between the office and the home. But if your work is your "passion," you'll be more likely to devote yourself to it, even if that means going home for dinner and then working long after the kids are in bed. But this seems to be the irony of office speak: Everyone makes fun of it, but managers love it, companies depend on it, and regular people willingly absorb it. As a linguist once said, "You can get people to think it's nonsense at the same time that you buy into it." In a workplace that's fundamentally indifferent to your life and its meaning, office speak can help you figure out how you relate to your work – and how your work defines who you are.

Many people talked of the 288,000 new jobs the Labor Department reported for June, along with the drop in the unemployment rate to 6.1 percent, as good news. And they were right. For now it appears the economy is creating jobs at a decent pace. We still have a long way to go to get back to full employment, but at least we are now finally moving forward at a faster pace. However, there is another important part of the jobs picture that was largely overlooked. There was a big jump in the number of people who report voluntarily working part-time. This figure is now 830,000 (4.4 percent) above its year ago level. Before explaining the connection to the Obamacare, it is worth making an important distinction. Many people who work part-time jobs actually want full-time jobs. They take part-time work because this is all they can get. An increase in involuntary part-time work is evidence of weakness in the labor market and it means that many people will be having a very hard time making ends meet. There was an increase in involuntary part-time in June, but the general direction has been down. Involuntary part-time employment is still far higher than before the recession, but it is down by 640,000 (7.9 percent) from its year ago level. We know the difference between voluntary and involuntary part-time employment because people tell us. The survey used by the Labor Department asks people if they worked less than 35 hours in the reference week. If the answer is "yes," they are classified as working part-time. The survey then asks whether they worked less than 35 hours in that week because they wanted to work less than full time or because they had no choice. They are only classified as voluntary part-time workers if they tell the survey taker they chose to work less than 35 hours a week. The issue of voluntary part-time relates to Obamacare because one of the main purposes was to allow people to get insurance outside of employment. For many people, especially those with serious health conditions or family members with serious health conditions, before Obamacare the only way to get insurance was through a job that provided health insurance. However, Obamacare has allowed more than 12 million people to either get insurance through Medicaid or the exchanges. These are people who may previously have felt the need to get a full-time job that provided insurance in order to cover themselves and their families. With Obamacare there is no longer a link between employment and insurance.

sections.directions: Part B Directions:Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

blocks.content: Some Old Truths to Help You Overcome Tough Times Unfortunately, life is not a bed of roses. We are going through life facing sad experiences. Moreover, we are grieving various kinds of loss: a friendship, a romantic relationship or a house. Hard times may hold you down at what usually seems like the most inopportune time, but you should remember that they won't last forever. When our time of mourning is over, we press forward, stronger with a greater understanding and respect for life. Furthermore, these losses make us mature and eventually move us toward future opportunities for growth and happiness. I want to share these old truths I've learned along the way.

Fear is both useful and harmful. This normal human reaction is used to protect us by signaling danger and preparing us to deal with it. Unfortunately, people create inner barriers with the help of exaggerating fears. My favorite actor Will Smith once said, "Fear is not real. It is a product of thoughts you create. Do not misunderstand me. Danger is very real. But fear is a choice." I do completely agree that fears are just the product of our luxuriant imagination.

If you are surrounded by problems and cannot stop thinking about the past, try to focus on the present moment. Many of us are weighed down by the past or anxious about the future. You may feel guilt over your past, but you are poisoning the present with the things and circumstances you cannot change. Value the present moment and remember how fortunate you are to be alive. Enjoy the beauty of the world around and keep your eyes open to see the possibilities before you. Happiness is not a point in the future and not a moment from the past, but a mindset that can be designed into the present.

Sometimes it is easy to feel bad because you are going through tough times. You can be easily caught up by life problems that you forget to pause and appreciate the things you have. Only strong people prefer to smile and value their life instead of crying and complaining about something.

No matter how isolated you might feel and how serious the situation is, you should always remember that you are not alone. Try to keep in mind that almost everyone respects and wants to help you if you are trying to make a good change in your life, especially your dearest and nearest people. You may have a circle of friends who provide constant good humor, help and companionship. If you have no friends or relatives, try to participate in several online communities, full of people who are always willing to share advice and encouragement.

Today many people find it difficult to trust their own opinion and seek balance by gaining objectivity from external sources. This way you devalue your opinion and show that you are incapable of managing your own life. When you are struggling to achieve something important you should believe in yourself and be sure that your decision is the best. You live in your skin, think your own thoughts, have your own values and make your own choices.
